problem_text: An observational hospital dataset of 50,000 patients shows that patients receiving treatment T had 25% lower one-year mortality than patients not receiving T. The analysis adjusted for age and sex, but treatment assignment was not randomized; disease severity, socioeconomic status, clinician choice, and several comorbidities are incompletely measured. Can this dataset by itself establish that treatment T causally reduces one-year mortality by 25%?

workers.role_task: Define the minimum evidence chain required before a causal operational claim can be promoted.
Classify what the observational association supports and identify missing evidence or assumptions.
Construct a plausible confounding or selection mechanism that could create the observed association without the claimed causal effect.
Produce a checkpoint-ready synthesis that preserves the association, the causal uncertainty, missing evidence, and residual risks.
State the causal identification assumptions or design conditions under which the observed effect could support a causal estimate.

hidden_answer_policy: The GVL wave receives only generic coaxial invariants, never task-specific causal-answer text.
